title: Where everyone sits after the move
variant: A plan drawn to scale, with names that appear as you zoom in
prompt: We have the new seating plan in a spreadsheet. Draw it as an actual floor plan so we can see what it looks like before the furniture goes in.
note: The plan shape: nothing is draggable, because the positions are measurements rather than opinions, and a reader who moves a desk here has broken the page's only claim. It is the file that uses semantic zoom for real work -- every desk name and room capacity carries `data-from`, so the fitted view is six zones and a count and the names arrive when you go looking for them. Every count on it is derived from the seating list, including the ones in the floor strip and beside each zone name, which is what stops a plan disagreeing with its own desks. The three findings are all statements about distance, which is the test of whether a plan earned being drawn: if none of them need the geometry, a table of names would have done. They are written in marker over the top, and the shapes are picked for what they sit on -- a bracket beside the meeting rooms, because a lasso is an ellipse and an ellipse round a rectangle either misses its corners or swallows the floor; rings round the free desks, sized to the desks themselves.
